item.title: Current Events - October 28, 2026
item.description:
October 28, 2026 (2026-10-28) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Houthi–Saudi conflict, Yemeni civil war
      • Saudi Arabia launches an airstrike at a market in Al Hazm, Al-Jawf Governorate, Yemen, killing 14 civilians and wounding ten more. (Xinhua)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis, Canada and the 2026 Iran war
    • The Bank of Canada raises its policy interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.5%, its first increase since July 2023, citing persistent inflation driven partly by higher oil and gasoline prices linked to the Iran war. (AFP)
  • Jio Platforms raises US$3.2 billion in India's largest-ever initial public offering (IPO), attracting about $77 billion in bids and becoming the country's most-subscribed IPO before its stock-market debut in Mumbai. (AFP via France 24)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season
    • At least three people are killed as Cyclone Arnab makes landfall in Andhra Pradesh, India. (DNA) (Reuters)
  • 2026 Toledo train collision
    • At least 68 people are killed and 179 injured during a collision between two high speed trains carrying over 500 passengers between Los Yébenes and Urda, in the Province of Toledo, Spain. (Sky News)

International relations

  • Rwanda–United States relations, Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict
    • The United States imposes sanctions on the Rwandan ministry of defence over its role in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, alleging that Rwanda is backing the M23 rebels to fight against Congolese forces. (Internazionale)

Law and crime

  • Attacks on Israeli embassies
    • A youth armed with two knives wounds a police officer outside the Israeli embassy in Belgrade, Serbia, before being shot and killed. (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 Japan Series
    • In baseball, the Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks defeats the Yokohama DeNA BayStars in four games to win its 13th Japan Series championship. (Kyodo News)

item.title: Current Events - October 21, 2026
item.description:
October 21, 2026 (2026-10-21) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • Houthi–Saudi conflict
        • October 2026 Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian airports
          • Two people are killed and eight others are injured in a Houthi attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia. (BBC News)
        • Saudi Arabia–United States relations
          • The U.S. Department of State orders non-emergency employees at its embassy in Riyadh to leave the country as Houthi attacks ramp up. (Al Jazeera)
        • Two people are killed and two others are injured by debris after a suspected Houthi drone is shot down near Shaybah oil field in Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia. (ABS-CBN News)
    • Gaza war
      • 2025 Gaza City offensive
        • The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and Shin Bet say that they have killed Musa Abd Muhammad Hamouda, a Hamas Nukhba forces militant that took part in planning the killing of four IDF soldiers in September 2025. (Ynetnews)
  • Haitian conflict
    • 2026 Croix-des-Bouquets gang ambush
      • Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele announces the start of a military operation to rescue four Air Force technicians. The technicians, attached to the international Gang Suppression Force, were taken hostage after gangs attacked their armored vehicle on 18 October. (Reuters)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • United States special envoy Steve Witkoff arrives in Saint Petersburg to talk with Russian president Vladimir Putin about potentially resolving the war with Ukraine. Putin states he would resume United States-mediated trilateral peace talks with Ukraine, on or after November 10. (Reuters) (Reuters)
      • American military veteran Stephen Hubbard, who was arrested by Russian authorities in 2022 during the Battle of Izium, is released from custody during the meeting between Putin and Witkoff. (AP) (BBC News)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
    • South Africa cuts fuel levies by R3.00 (US$0.18) per litre of diesel and R1.50 ($0.09) per litre of petrol from November 4 to December 1 after fuel prices reach record highs. (AFP)
  • The North Sea Transition Authority (NSTA) of the United Kingdom approves production from the Jackdaw gas field after energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh authorized the NSTA to grant consent, allowing operator Adura to begin supplying gas by late October. (UPI)

International relations

  • Indonesia, Pakistan, Qatar, and Turkey jointly sign the Badr Memorandum of Understanding, a major agreement to deepen their defence industry cooperation. The agreement aims to support joint military production projects and strengthen cooperation in technical training, research, and development. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)
  • Ireland's Dáil Éireann approves legislation removing the requirement for United Nations authorization before deploying more than 12 Defence Forces personnel overseas for peacekeeping missions, while retaining approval by the government and parliament. (France 24)

Law and crime

  • 2026 anti-immigrant movement and xenophobia in South Africa
    • A foreign national is beaten to death by a crowd in Durban, South Africa. (BBC News)
  • 2026 Italian unrest
    • Italian interior minister Matteo Piantedosi announces a crackdown on truck drivers and farmers protesting in southern Italy over the past month against high fuel prices by blocking highways and transport routes, reporting that they have identified 1,339 individuals, reported 71, and fined 242. (Ansa in Italian)
  • Cross-strait relations
    • Taiwanese prosecutors indict five people for allegedly accepting money and planning to injure Huang Yihao, an anti-Chinese Communist Party comedian in New Taipei City. (AP)
  • Lawsuits involving Meta Platforms
    • A district judge in New Mexico, United States, orders Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found it guilty of misleading Facebook users about privacy violations, marking its largest fine ever. (Al Jazeera)
  • Over 80 Americans, British citizens, and Israelis are detained by Israeli soldiers in the Israel-occupied West Bank, including U.S. House of Representatives candidate Brad Lander. (The Guardian)
  • A Tunisian military court sentences politician and businesswoman Olfa Hamdi to four years in prison on state security charges linked to social media posts, including accusations of inciting military personnel to disobey orders. (AFP via Arab News)

Politics and elections

  • Gen Z protests
    • 2026 European unrest
      • Thousands of students and teachers march through Athens, Thessaloniki, and Patras in Greece to protest against the rising cost of living, calling for affordable student housing and more state investment in education. (AP)
  • 2026 Quebec general election, St-Pierre Plamondon ministry
    • Paul St-Pierre Plamondon is sworn in as the 34th premier of Quebec, Canada, following the Parti Québécois's victory in the general election. (The Globe and Mail)

Science and technology

  • 2022–2026 video game industry layoffs
    • Leveraged buyout of Electronic Arts
      • American video game publisher Electronic Arts, which was recently bought-out by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, announces the closing of its Canadian studio BioWare. (Kotaku)
  • Node.js releases three security updates to 10 different vulnerabilities, including 4 deemed high-severity, which affect how it handles DNS resolution, TLS handshakes, and Brotli decoding. (Heise Online)

Sports

  • 2026 Canadian Championship
    • 2026 Canadian Championship final
      • In association football, Forge FC defeats CF Montréal in a penalty shoot-out to become the first Canadian Premier League team to win a Canadian Championship. (CBC)
  • 2026 U.S. Open Cup
    • 2026 U.S. Open Cup final
      • In association football, St. Louis City SC defeats Columbus Crew in a penalty shoot-out to win the U.S. Open Cup, earning the club its first trophy since beginning play in 2023. (ESPN)

item.title: Current Events - October 27, 2026
item.description:
October 27, 2026 (2026-10-27) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • The Persian Gulf Strait Authority says that vessels belonging to South Korean shipping company Sinokor would face legal action beginning on 1 November. (Reuters)
    • Gaza genocide
      • Three people, including a child, are killed in an Israeli airstrike against a tent in Khan Yunis, Gaza Strip. (Asharq Al-Awsat)
  • War on drugs
    • Colombian conflict
      • A bomb explodes near a bridge in Cúcuta, Colombia, at the border with Venezuela, injuring four police officers. (AP)
    • Operation Southern Spear, United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
      • The United States launches an airstrike against an alleged drug boat in the Pacific Ocean, killing five people. (AP)
  • Ethiopian civil conflict, Persecution of Christians in Ethiopia
    • The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church reports that at least 60 Christians have been killed in attacks in Oromia, Ethiopia, over the last week. (Reuters)
  • Nigerian bandit conflict
    • The casualty toll from the massacre by unknown gunmen four days ago in Taraba State, Nigeria, increases to 62 people killed and 52 more wounded. (AP)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • The casualty toll from yesterday's drone strike at a market Nyala, South Darfur, Sudan, increases to over 100 people killed and 112 more injured. (Reuters)

Business and economy

  • AI bubble
    • China's Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market index, which focuses on science and technology companies, plummets 40% in less than four months. (Reuters)

Arts and culture

  • Eurovision Song Contest 2027
    • Netherlands in the Eurovision Song Contest 2027
      • Netherlands Public Broadcasting (NPO) withdraws the Netherlands from the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest over concerns about Israel's participation, after AVROTROS withdrew in August and NPO failed to find another broadcaster. (AP)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season
    • Indian authorities order nearly 100,000 people to evacuate parts of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha as Cyclone Arnab approaches, with the India Meteorological Department forecasting landfall as a very severe cyclonic storm. (AFP via RFI)
  • Four people are killed, two are missing and several homes are destroyed during floods in Haiti and the Dominican Republic. (AP)
  • A construction site is hit by a tornado in Kepez, Antalya, Turkey, killing four workers and injuring another. (AP)

Health and environment

  • 2025 in climate change
    • The World Meteorological Organization reports that global concentrations of carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide reached record highs in 2025, with carbon dioxide averaging 426.8 parts per million. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • Crime in El Salvador
    • A Salvadoran court issues an order to release former president Antonio Saca from prison after the end of his 10-year sentence for corruption. (La Prensa Gráfica in Spanish)
  • Gaza war protests at Columbia University
    • Algerian-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil returns to Columbia University in New York City, United States, after immigration authorities detained him for more than three months over his role in pro-Palestinian campus protests before a federal judge ordered his release. (AFP)
  • Immigration to Nigeria
    • Nigerian police arrest 34 foreigners, including 16 Cameroonians and 18 Nigeriens, suspected of engaging in "illicit activities" in Benue State. The commissioner opens an investigation into their immigration status. (Daily Trust)
  • Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil for the United States, despite orders to surrender his passports to the Federal Police, two days after his defeat in the presidential election runoffs to incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The government subsequently cancels Bolsonaro's passports, while the U.S. grants him and his family visas. (AFP) (Reuters)
  • An Egyptian court orders independent news website Mada Masr to close after convicting editor-in-chief Lina Attalah of operating without a licence. The court also fines her E£3,000,000 (US$53,500) and orders the outlet's equipment confiscated. (DW)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 French fuel protests, 2026 French student protests
    • The French Senate passes a bill that would make people who knowingly participate in violent protest groups jointly liable for up to €10,000 (US$11,118) in damage and allow authorities to seize certain welfare payments. The bill heads to the National Assembly for a vote. (AFP via The Straits Times)
  • 2026 Israeli legislative election
    • Israelis vote to elect the 120 members of the Knesset. (BBC News) (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - October 20, 2026
item.description:
October 20, 2026 (2026-10-20) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Sudanese civil war
    • Abyei border conflict
      • Amiet market massacre
        • The death toll in the market drone attack in Abyei on the border of South Sudan and Sudan yesterday rises to 220. (Sudans Post)
    • Blue Nile campaign
      • The Sudanese Army says that they have repelled an attack by the Rapid Support Forces and Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North (SPLM–N) on the Blue Nile state. (Sudan Tribune)
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
      • The Rapid Support Forces launches a drone strike on a power plant in Tendelti in Sudan's White Nile State, knocking out the main transition line connecting North Kordofan. (Sudan Tribune)

Disasters and accidents

  • At least 14 people are killed and 20 others are injured after a bus and a truck collide head-on in Natore District, Bangladesh. (Xinhua)
  • Twelve people are killed and 30 others are injured after a bus crashes into a truck near Cairo, Egypt. (Xinhua)
  • A leak of glycidyl methacrylate from a chemical tank at the terminal in Toledo, Ohio, United States, forces nearly 1,000 residents to evacuate and prompts shelter-in-place orders for more than 50,000 people in Toledo. (Associated Press) (EPA)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • Nigeria announces its first case of Ebola virus in the epidemic. (The Guardian)

International relations

  • Libya–Turkey relations
    • Libya (GNA)–Turkey maritime deal
      • Libya's eastern-based House of Representatives approves a 2019 maritime boundary agreement with Turkey and repeals two 2020 decisions that rejected the accord. (Reuters)
  • South Korea–Ukraine relations
    • South Korea withdraws additional embassy staff from Ukraine following a dispute over two captured North Korean soldiers who were transferred to South Korea. (AFP via RFI)
  • Houthi–Saudi conflict, Saudi Arabia–United Kingdom relations
    • United Kingdom says it will deploy RAF Typhoons to help Saudis defend against Houthi attacks. (BBC News) (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 17 October riots
      • Police arrest a 34-year-old man for the arson attack on the Hôtel de Ville in Limoges, Haute-Vienne, France. (BBC)
  • 2022 San Antonio migrant deaths
    • A United States federal judge sentences a Guatemalan national to 30 years in prison for helping organize a 2022 migrant-smuggling operation in San Antonio, Texas, that left 53 migrants dead and 11 injured. (AFP via France 24)
  • Pakistan arrests a man for selling fake Postage stamps in the United States that resulted in a $126 million loss to the U.S. Postal Service. (BBC News) (Dawn)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Romanian political crisis
    • The Parliament of Romania appoints Luca Niculescu as the new Prime Minister, succeeding Ilie Bolojan who resigned amid a politicial crisis. (Reuters)
  • Malaysia's Registrar of Societies deregisters the opposition coalition Perikatan Nasional, citing internal disputes and breaches of the constitution, preventing its component parties from contesting forthcoming elections under a common coalition banner. (Reuters)

Science and technology

  • Japanese space program
    • JAXA launches the Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft from the Tanegashima Space Center toward Phobos aboard an H3 rocket, aiming to collect at least 10 grams of surface material from the Martian moon and return the samples to Earth in 2031. (Reuters)
  • PHP2Shell
    • A critical vulnerability in PHP allowing for remote code execution is discovered, causing many websites to temporarily go offline while a security update is pushed the following day. (NBC News)
  • Indian certificate authority eMudhra has its private keys compromised, revealing that some of them were extremely insecure single digit numerals. Major web browser developers Mozilla, Google, and Apple subsequently block the certificates. (The Register)

item.title: Current Events - October 22, 2026
item.description:
October 22, 2026 (2026-10-22) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reports that seven oil tankers have been hit in the Strait of Hormuz. (Al Jazeera)
    • Yemeni civil war, Al-Qaeda insurgency in Yemen
      • Al-Qaeda gunmen ambush Yemeni Armed Forces soldiers at a mountainous area in the Shabwah Governorate, killing two soldiers and wounding several more. (Xinhua)
  • Haitian conflict
    • 2026 Croix-des-Bouquets gang ambush
      • El Salvador deploys 100 special forces soldiers to Haiti to assist in the search efforts for the four missing Air Force technicians attached to the Gang Suppression Force. (AP)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Blue Nile campaign
      • The Sudanese Armed Forces recaptures two strategic areas in Sudan's Blue Nile state, including the Bukuri base in Ad-Damazin. (Sudan Tribune)

Arts and culture

  • British singer Raye wins the 2026 Mercury Prize for her album This Music May Contain Hope. (Billboard)
  • The European Parliament awards its 2026 Sakharov Prize to the International Criminal Court and its officials for their work in global justice and upholding international law. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026–27 European windstorm season
    • At least four people are killed and one other is injured by flooding caused by Storm Adam in Bouches-du-Rhône, France. (BBC News)
  • 2026 Tibet earthquake
    • A Mw 7.0 earthquake strikes Tibet, with an epicenter in Nagqu, killing 16 people and wounding 32 more. (Al Jazeera)
  • At least six people are killed and 25 others are injured when a bus collides with a tree in Manendragarh-Chirmiri-Bharatpur district, Chhattisgarh, India. (Xinhua)

Health and environment

  • France reports the first human case of the livestock Shamonda virus in a patient who died after being hospitalized with an unrelated condition. (Reuters)

International relations

  • Canada–Turkey relations, Free trade agreements of Canada, Free trade agreements of Turkey
    • Canada and Turkey open negotiations for a free trade agreement during Canadian prime minister Mark Carney's visit to Ankara. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 United Nations Secretary-General selection
    • Emirati diplomat Lana Nusseibeh announces her candidacy for Secretary-General of the United Nations. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Corruption in Ecuador
    • Ecuadorian opposition leader and former presidential candidate Luisa González is arrested over allegations of money laundering in campaign financing. (Reuters)
  • LGBTQ rights in Guatemala
    • A Guatemalan court sentences seven former police officers to prison terms of up to 60 years for offenses related to the 2024 torture and killing of a gay couple at a police station. (AFP via France 24)

Science and technology

  • The Finnish Government grants Posiva an operating license for the Onkalo spent nuclear fuel repository in Eurajoki, making it the world's first licensed deep geological disposal facility for spent nuclear fuel. (AFP via France 24)

Sports

  • 2026 World Artistic Gymnastics Championships
    • In artistic gymnastics, Japan's Daiki Hashimoto wins his fourth consecutive men's all-around title at the 2026 World Championships in Rotterdam, Netherlands, finishing ahead of China's Zhang Boheng and Japan's Shinnosuke Oka. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026-27 NFL season
    • In American football, the Chicago Bears receive an illegal forward handing penalty in a game against the New England Patriots, the first time in 16 years that the penalty has been handed out. (CBS Sports)
  • 2028 FIFA Women's Club World Cup
    • In women's association football, FIFA announces that the United States will host the inaugural FIFA Women's Club World Cup in 2028. (ESPN)
  • The Athletics Integrity Unit bans Ethiopian marathon runner Ruti Aga for six years after she tested positive for methylprednisolone and submitted false information and a forged prescription during an investigation. (AFP via France 24)

item.title: Current Events - October 15, 2026
item.description:
October 15, 2026 (2026-10-15) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Yemeni civil war
    • Houthi–Saudi conflict
      • Saudi Arabia says that it has intercepted a missile intended for Medina. However, the Houthis denied launching a missile at the city. (The Hill) (France 24)
    • The Houthis launch missiles against Al-Maashiq Palace, headquarters of the Presidential Leadership Council and official residence of President Rashad al-Alimi, in Aden, Yemen, killing five people and injuring 16. No member of the council is harmed in the attack. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)

Business and economy

  • China–North Korea relations
    • The New Yalu River Bridge connecting Dandong, China, and Sinuiju, North Korea, opens following a 12-year delay. (BBC News) (NK News)
  • The European Central Bank authorizes UniCredit to raise its stake in Commerzbank above 30% without an upper limit, allowing the Italian bank to proceed toward taking control of the German lender. (The Eastern Herald)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Peshawar school roof collapse
    • A roof collapses at a school in Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killing 34 students and a teacher, and injuring 50 more people. (BBC News)
  • 2026 Indonesia wildfires
    • Four people are killed fighting wildfires in Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park in East Java, Indonesia, after flames and thick smoke trapped them. Two others suffer serious burns. (AFP)
  • Seven people are missing after a San Marino-flagged tanker catches fire off the coast of Romania amid recent drone attacks on merchant shipping in the Black Sea. Search and rescue operations are underway to locate the missing crew members. (Politico)

Health and environment

  • The United Kingdom declares a severe drought in Cornwall, Devon, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex, and West Sussex after prolonged low rainfall left more than 80% of England in drought and major reservoirs below 20% capacity. (AFP)

International relations

  • Germany–Iran relations, Antisemitism in 21st-century Germany, Iranian external operations
    • A court in Hamburg, Germany, sentences a Danish national to eight years and six months in prison and an Afghan national to four years and six months in prison for plotting to assassinate Josef Schuster, the president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, on behalf of Iran. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Silver Rail Elementary School shooting
    • Three children and a teacher are killed in a mass school shooting at the Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, United States. Two other people are wounded. The perpetrator, a 16-year-old male, is shot and killed by a bystander. (AP) (The Guardian)
  • Capital punishment in the United States
    • U.S. president Donald Trump announces that the Department of Defense has reversed its plan to livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, the perpetrator of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, scheduled for December 3. (AFP via France 24) (AP)
  • Argentine police arrest at least 25 people after clashes during a university funding protest in Buenos Aires, while eight police officers are injured. (AFP via France 24)
  • Northern Irish politician and former Democratic Unionist Party leader Jeffrey Donaldson is sentenced to 15 years in prison for child sexual abuse and rape. The offences occurred between 1985 and 2008. (AP) (BBC News)

Science and technology

  • Astronomers discover the first green star, WD J1330+6435, according to a study published by RAS Techniques and Instruments. (Popular Science)
  • At the General Conference on Weights and Measures, the International Bureau of Weights and Measures votes to abolish future leap seconds and make Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) continuous, starting 20 May 2027. To account for future differences between UTC and International Atomic Time, a leap hour will be observed as needed. (The Guardian) (Scientific American)

Sports

  • 2026 Major League Baseball season
    • In baseball, the Milwaukee Brewers sweep the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS to advance to the 2026 World Series, their first since 1982. (ESPN)

item.title: Current Events - October 25, 2026
item.description:
October 25, 2026 (2026-10-25) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Houthi–Saudi conflict, Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Houthi attacks on Saudi airports
        • Saudi-led coalition air defences intercept a Houthi ballistic missile and two drones targeting Riyadh Province as King Khalid International Airport resumes limited operations after a two-week closure caused by earlier Houthi attacks. (AFP via ABS-CBN News)
    • Gaza war
      • Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
        • Three staff members are killed and eight students are wounded in an Israeli airstrike against the Islamic University of Gaza in Gaza City. Four other Palestinians are also killed in more airstrikes in the Gaza Strip. (AFP via Dawn)
  • Colombian conflict
    • The Colombian government announces that a military operation in El Tambo, Cauca, in the previous days resulted in the killing of ten National Liberation Army's members, including two key leaders. (AP)
  • Islamist insurgency in Niger, Foreign relations of Algeria, Foreign relations of Niger
    • Algeria's parliament approves the deployment of army units to Madama, Niger, to protect energy infrastructure, marking Algeria's first foreign military deployment since 1973. (BBC News)

Business and economy

  • Western Sydney Airport in New South Wales, Australia, commences passenger operations as Greater Sydney's second airport. (The Guardian)

Disasters and accidents

  • Twenty-four people are killed and 24 more are injured after a bus collides with a truck on a highway in Makueni County, Kenya. (AP)
  • Eighty-three people are injured, including seven seriously, in a bus crash in Fogars de Montclús, Catalonia, Spain. (AP)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • The Nigerian health ministry expands contact tracing after confirming an imported Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja, identifying at least 44 contacts while investigating additional people who may have been exposed and strengthening infection-control measures. (AFP via RFI)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Brazilian general election
    • Brazilians vote in the second round of presidential elections between incumbent left-wing president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of the Workers' Party and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party. (AP) (Reuters)
    • In a vote of 52% to 48%, Lula defeats Bolsonaro to win re-election for a fourth non-consecutive term. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Bulgarian presidential election
    • Bulgarians vote in the first round of the presidential election. Incumbent Iliana Iotova wins and will face former acting prime minister Andrey Gyurov in a second round due to record low turnout and no candidate having a majority of the vote. (AP via CNN) (Reuters)
  • 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
    • Serbians vote for all seats in the National Assembly in a snap election, amid the student-led protests against the incumbent United Serbia government. (AP)
    • The Student List wins the election with 53% of the vote, with former president Aleksandar Vučić conceding defeat. (RFE/RL) (Reuters)
  • 2027 French presidential election
    • French politician Marine Le Pen, leader of the far-right National Rally party, announces her presidential campaign. (Reuters)
  • Crisis in Venezuela
    • Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado announces she has returned to Venezuela from exile. (CNN)

Sports

  • 2026 NASCAR Cup Series
    • 2026 YellaWood 500
      • In auto racing, American driver Kyle Larson of Hendrick Motorsports wins the YellaWood 500 at the Talladega Superspeedway in Alabama, winning his first NASCAR Cup Series race at the circuit. (ESPN)
  • 2027 Dakar Rally
    • In rally raid, Dakar Rally organizers move the 2027 event from Saudi Arabia because of security concerns regarding the conflict with the Houthis. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 LPGA Tour
    • In golf, Japan's Yuri Yoshida wins her first LPGA Tour title at the BMW Ladies Championship in South Jeolla Province, South Korea, finishing ahead of Australia's Minjee Lee and South Korea's Kim Sei-young. (AFP)
  • International sporting sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
    • The International Weightlifting Federation awards Moscow, Russia, the hosting rights to the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships, making it the first IOC-recognised sports federation to grant Russia hosting rights for a world championship since the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine. (AFP via The Straits Times)

item.title: Current Events - October 18, 2026
item.description:
October 18, 2026 (2026-10-18) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
      • Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reports that an oil tanker has caught on fire and exploded in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz after striking a naval mine. (Middle East Eye)
  • Haitian conflict
    • El Salvador–Haiti relations
      • Armed gang members ambush Salvadoran Air Force personnel serving with Haiti's Gang Suppression Force in Port-au-Prince, using gunfire and explosives. Four Salvadoran service members remain missing after escaping their burning armored vehicle. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • A truck loses control and runs over devotees outside a temple in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, India, killing at least 13 and injuring nearly 40 others. (AFP via Dawn) (The Indian Express)
  • At least eight people are killed and eight others are injured after a mortar shell explosion in Zawiya, Libya. (Xinhua)
  • A light aircraft crashes into a dry riverbed in Kondariotissa, Pieria, Greece. Two people are killed. (Xinhua)

Health and environment

  • Equatorial Guinea announces that it will expand its program combating malaria to the mainland and Annobón. The program has already heavily reduced malaria cases on Bioko Island. (The Independent)

International relations

  • Cross-strait relations
    • The Taiwanese coast guard drives away 16 Chinese coast guard, research, and fishing vessels operating near Taiwan and the Pratas Island, including some that entered restricted waters. (AFP via The Hindu)
  • Free trade agreements of Vietnam
    • Vietnam signs a free trade agreement with the European Free Trade Association (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland) that reduces or eliminates tariffs on industrial, agricultural, and fish products and covers services, intellectual property, and sustainable development. (AFP)

Politics and elections

  • Water scarcity in Mexico
    • Protests continue for the second week in Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico, over water shortages and widespread contamination. A study in June found that at least 93% of households' water systems contained no residual chlorine, but had elevated levels of lead, mercury, nitrates, and E. coli. (Reuters) (Türkiye)
  • The Iranian parliament appoints Mehrdad Akhlaghi as Minister of Defence, replacing acting minister Majid Ebn-e-Reza. (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - October 24, 2026
item.description:
October 24, 2026 (2026-10-24) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Houthi–Saudi conflict, Yemeni civil war
      • Saudi Arabia launches airstrikes against a residential building and a cement factory in Hamdan district, Yemen, killing ten people and wounding many more. (Tempo)
  • Gaza war
    • 2026 West Bank lockdown
      • The Israeli military raids 15 cities in the occupied West Bank, arresting several Palestinians, forcing over 2,000 from their homes, and destroying a three-storey building in Hebron. (Al Jazeera) (Al Jazeera)
  • Nigerian bandit conflict
    • Unknown gunmen attack a village in Taraba State, Nigeria, killing at least ten people. Locals place the death toll at 20, while Amnesty International claims at least 40. (Al Jazeera)
  • 2026 Karak church shooting
    • Two people succumb to their injuries sustained the day before during a mass shooting at a Greek Orthodox Church in Karak Governorate, Jordan, bringing the toll to nine killed and 40 injured. (CNN)
  • Unknown gunmen open fire against a group of medics in Bafwasende, Democratic Republic of the Congo, while responding to an Ebola case amid the ongoing emergency, killing a nurse and injuring a health worker. (AP)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Pacific typhoon season
    • At least one person is killed and 527 others are injured as Typhoon Champi swept near Taiwan. (DW)
  • Six people are killed and another is injured when a passenger train collides with a minibus in Jewish Autonomous Oblast, Russia. (Reuters)
  • Five people are killed in a fire at the market place of Sorsogon City, Philippines. (PNA)
  • Two people are killed and over 2,000 others are displaced by flooding in Chaco and Corrientes, Argentina. (AA)

Law and crime

  • Catholic Church sex abuse cases in the United States
    • Survivors of sexual abuse by Catholic clergy reach a settlement with the Archdiocese of New York in the United States, which will see the archdiocese paying at least $250,000 to around 1,300 plaintiffs, totaling over $800 million. (DW)
  • Five people are killed and three more are injured in a suspected gang-related mass shooting at a residence in Lavender Hill, Cape Flats, South Africa. (Smile 90.4FM)
  • Eleven people, including six children, are injured in a mass shooting at Bragg Memorial Stadium in Tallahassee, Florida, United States. (CNN)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 2026 French fuel protests
      • The Yellow vests hold a second wave of mass demonstrations across France. About 410,000 people participate and over 1,000 people are arrested. (The Guardian) (France 24)
      • About 110,000 protesters march in Paris, France. (France 24)
      • Rioters in Paris attack police with projectiles, but are dispersed with tear gas and water cannons. A gendarmerie helicopter is deployed to locate remaining rioters. (France 24)
      • Party leader Marine Le Pen holds the National Rally congress in Orléans, France. Protesters, including left-wing politicians, marched in opposition. (CBS) (Euronews)
    • 2026 Italian unrest
      • A new wave of protests is held across Italy. Clashes are reported in Bologna, Turin, Rome and Florence. Protests are also held in Milan, Naples, Padua and Bari. (Rai News)
    • Flamingo Revolution
      • Anti-government protests break out in Tirana, Albania. Various government buildings are attacked. (The Guardian)
    • At least 25,000 people gather in Madrid, Spain, in support of the country's state pension fund amid the general election in November. (Al Jazeera)
    • A student protest in Barcelona, Spain, ends in riots, looting and clashes with the police, resulting in 128 arrests. (Euronews)
  • 2026 British Columbia general election
    • The Conservative Party of British Columbia wins the provincial snap election in Canada, returning to government for the first time in nearly a century and ending nine years of New Democratic Party (NDP) rule. Premier David Eby resigns as NDP leader. (CBC) (Reuters)
  • Thousands of Israelis rally in Hostages Square in Tel Aviv to protest against the government, prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet, and the continuation of the Gaza war. (Al Jazeera)

item.title: Current Events - October 17, 2026
item.description:
October 17, 2026 (2026-10-17) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • Egypt–Saudi Arabia relations, Houthi–Saudi conflict
        • Egyptian president Abdel Fattah El-Sisi states that Egypt will take all necessary steps to protect and defend Saudi Arabia should the latter so desire. (AFP via Arab News)
    • Gaza war
      • Israeli settler violence
        • Masked Israeli settlers attack a group of European diplomats, including the Belgian consul general, French and Polish diplomats, and Catholic representatives visiting Taybeh in the occupied West Bank, Palestine. (AP)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Kolkata Durga Puja crowd crush
    • At least 17 people are killed and 25 others are injured in a crowd crush at a pandal in Kolkata, West Bengal, India. (Hindustan Times) (Sky News)
  • CFB Wainwright fire
    • An explosion and wildfire occurs at the CFB Wainwright, a Canadian Armed Forces base in Alberta. Four people are killed and dozens more injured. (CBC News) (CTV News)
  • Ten tourists are killed and nine others sustain injuries after a resort catches fire in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh. (AA)
  • Eight people are killed and eight others are injured after a minibus carrying 23 passengers plunges into a drain along the Delhi–Mumbai Expressway near Kota, Rajasthan, India. (The Times of India)
  • A Piper Tomahawk II aircraft crashes near Drymen, Stirling, Scotland, killing the two people on board. (BBC News)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • Kenya confirms four additional cases of Bundibugyo ebolavirus, including three health workers who treated Kenya's first patient and one of his relatives, raising the national total to seven. All four are already in quarantine. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 2026 French student protests
      • 17 October riots
        • Over 500,000 people take part in protests across France, according to the national trade union confederation, while clashes and riots erupt in large cities. (FranceInfo)
        • Protesters force their way into Marseille's town hall and vandalize the interior before being dispersed. (CNews)
        • In Lille, protesters storm the city hall and damage the premises prior to being removed by security forces. (Ouest-France)
        • Dozens of shops are looted across major French cities amid widespread rioting and civil unrest. (BFMTV)
      • The Hôtel de Ville in Limoges is partially destroyed by fire. (Le Parisien in French)
    • 2026 French fuel protests
      • Yellow vests activists hold mass demonstrations across France against rising fuel prices and join the student protests. (Al Jazeera)
  • 2026 anti-CEC protests
    • A court in New Delhi, India, orders the release of Cockroach Janta Party founder and activist Abhijeet Dipke on a peace bond, one day after police detained him while he was heading to a protest against the Election Commission of India. (AFP via France 24)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Czech Senate election
    • In Czechia, opposition parties win 22 of the contested 27 seats in the Senate. The lead party of prime minister Andrej Babiš's government, ANO 2011, comes in third place. The election is the first time in the country's history where governing parties did not win a single seat in a senatorial election. (AP)
  • Protests against Donald Trump
    • The fourth round of No Kings protests are held across the United States against president Donald Trump and his administration and to encourage early voting ahead of the upcoming midterm elections. (AFP) (USA Today)

Sports

  • 2026–27 NHL season
    • In ice hockey, the Florida Panthers become the first team in the National Hockey League to record a natural hat trick in three consecutive games. (The Athletic via The New York Times)

item.title: Current Events - October 26, 2026
item.description:
October 26, 2026 (2026-10-26) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war, Yemeni civil war
      • Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war, Saudi Arabia in the 2026 Iran war, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
        • Senior officials representing the members of the Mecca Defence Alliance, including Pakistani military chief Asim Munir, Saudi defense minister Khalid bin Salman Al Saud, and Turkish intelligence director İbrahim Kalın, meet with Iranian leadership, including President Masoud Pezeshkian, in Tehran to discuss efforts to de-escalate the 2026 Iran war and the Yemeni civil war. (Al Jazeera) (France 24)
    • Gaza war
      • Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
        • Israel launches an airstrike against a tent for displaced people in Khan Yunis, Gaza Strip, killing four Palestinians, including a child, and wounding many more. (Al Jazeera)
      • The Israel Defense Forces says that they have killed four Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad militants in the Gaza Strip over the weekend. (The Jerusalem Post)
    • Egypt–Saudi Arabia relations, Houthi–Saudi conflict, Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Houthi attacks on Saudi airports
        • Egypt's parliament authorizes President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to provide military support to Saudi Arabia if requested amid Houthi attacks in Saudi territory. (AFP via France 24)
  • Somali Civil War
    • Diplomatic and humanitarian efforts in the Somali Civil War
      • The United Nations (UN) announces it will conclude its support for the Transitional Assistance Mission to support the Somali federal government by October 31. The UN will continue supporting Somalia through other smaller agencies. (AA)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
      • Twenty-one people are killed and 40 more injured in a drone strike in Nyala, Sudan. (Al Jazeera)
      • More drone strikes by the Rapid Support Forces are reported across power stations in southeast Sudan, cutting power across the region. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Karak church shooting
    • The three gunmen who carried out a mass shooting at a Greek Orthodox Church in Karak Governorate, Jordan, are wounded and arrested after a shootout with security forces at an abandoned building. (BBC News)
    • The Jordanian Armed Forces announces that it has carried out airstrikes against alleged positions of the Islamic State in various areas of Syria's Daraa Governorate and Suwayda Governorate, reporting that the gunmen are linked to the group, claiming the killing of 20 militants. Seven civilians are confirmed killed, including three children and an elderly man. (Al Jazeera) (Internazionale)
    • The Syrian transitional government announces the closure of the Nasib Border Crossing with Jordan, suspending passenger and commercial traffic in both directions, after reporting that the airstrikes were not coordinated. (AA)

Arts and culture

  • Dictionary.com says maxxing has been named its word of the year for 2026 following a surge in its use across social media. (BBC News)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026–27 European windstorm season
    • Two people are killed and around 90,000 more are left without electricity after the impact of Storm Boelo in Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland, and northern England. (AA)

Law and crime

  • Brazilian police orders senator Flávio Bolsonaro to surrender his passports after Supreme Federal Court justice Alexandre de Moraes barred him from leaving Brazil, one day after Bolsonaro lost the runoff of the general election to incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. (Firstpost) (SBS News)
  • A Swiss court convicts former Belarusian security officer Yuri Harauski over the 1999 abduction of businessman Anatol Krasouski, later killed, and gives him a two-year suspended sentence. He is acquitted over Yury Zacharanka's enforced disappearance. (Reuters)
  • The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation announces they have arrested nine people involved in Nigerian scam centers, as part of an international operation targeting organised crime in Nigeria, locating $11 million in funds purloined by the scammers. (OCCRP)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 2026 Spanish housing protests
      • Protests and riots are held in Bilbao, Spain, after and during a political event hosted by far-right commentator Vito Quiles. At least nine people are arrested. (El Constitucional)

Sports

  • 2026 Ballon d'Or
    • In association football, English player Harry Kane wins the men's Ballon d'Or for the first time, while Spanish player Alexia Putellas receives the women's award for a record-tying third time. (CNN)

item.title: Current Events - October 19, 2026
item.description:
October 19, 2026 (2026-10-19) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Sudanese civil war
    • Abyei border conflict
      • Amiet market massacre
        • A drone strike kills at least 73 people at a market in the disputed Abyei area between South Sudan and Sudan. (Reuters)
    • Rapid Support Forces atrocities in Khartoum
      • Three children are killed in an alleged Rapid Support Forces drone strike in Khartoum, Sudan. (AP)
  • Yemeni civil war
    • 2026 Yemen offensives
      • 2026 Shabwah missile attack
        • A missile attack by the Houthis kills 58 soldiers and injure over 200 at a training center in Shabwah Governorate, Yemen. There are 14 missing. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • Mediterranean Sea migrant smuggling
    • Twelve migrants, including an infant, are killed when two separate speedboats capsize off the coast of the Lesbos and Samos islands in Greece. (AP)
  • Fourteen miners are killed and seven more injured when an open pit gold mine collapses in Nariño Department, Colombia. (AP)

International relations

  • Andorra–European Union relations, San Marino–European Union relations, Potential enlargement of the European Union
    • Andorra and San Marino each sign an association agreement with the European Union. (The Brussels Times)
  • Gaza Strip famine, Palestine and the United Nations
    • The World Food Programme cuts monthly food aid for about 500,000 people in the Gaza Strip because of funding shortages, reducing the number of recipients from 1.6 million to 1.1 million. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • Cuba–United States relations
    • 1996 shootdown of Brothers to the Rescue aircraft, United States embargo against Cuba
      • A judge in Miami-Dade County, Florida, United States, issues a no-bail bond arrest warrant for former Cuban president Raúl Castro after Florida attorney general James Uthmeier charged Castro with conspiracy to commit first-degree murder by directing spies to infiltrate Brothers to the Rescue and ordering the attack on their planes in 1996. (Al Jazeera)
  • Israeli settler violence
    • Israel Police arrest 10 people in the occupied West Bank over attacks on American photojournalist Heidi Levine and the mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries, France, who were travelling with European diplomats, and seize vehicles and other evidence during raids. (AFP via France 24) (Reuters)
  • Shakahola Forest incident
    • A Kenyan court convicts Good News International Ministries leader Paul Nthenge Mackenzie of murdering 190 children and an adult whose deaths were linked to starvation in Shakahola Forest. (Reuters)
  • Independent Australian MP Helen Haines is deliberately hit by a car outside her office in Wangaratta, Victoria. Police arrest the car's driver, while Haines is airlifted to a hospital. Haines later had both her legs amputated. (AFP) (The Guardian) (Reuters)
  • A teacher and a student are injured in a stabbing attack at a school in Bistrița, Romania. The 13-year-old suspect is arrested. (Reuters)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Alberta referendums, 2026 Alberta independence referendum
    • Albertans vote on ten referendums, including one to decide if Alberta should seek separation from Canada. (Reuters)
    • Albertan voters reject pursuing a future independence referendum, with more than three-quarters supporting the province remaining in Canada. (BBC News)

item.title: Current Events - October 23, 2026
item.description:
October 23, 2026 (2026-10-23) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • 2026 drone incidents in Romania
      • A merchant ship is hit by drones of unknown origins in the Romanian Black Sea, killing a crew member and leaving three more missing. Nine people are rescued. (Turkiye Today)
    • Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Blockade of Oleshky, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • The U.S. government says that Russia and Ukraine reached a humanitarian ceasefire agreement in Oleshky brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump. The ceasefire will take effect on Thursday. (Reuters)
      • Russia and Ukraine confirm the ceasefire agreement for Oleshky, with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy stating that peace talks will begin next month. (The Moscow Times) (Kyiv Independent)
    • Ukrainian police detain a 17-year-old girl suspected of helping Russia's Federal Security Service send methadone-laced capsules to Ukrainian soldiers, which killed two in Zhytomyr Oblast and allegedly targeting four others. (AFP via RFI)
  • Gaza war
    • 2026 West Bank lockdown
      • Israeli forces launch a multi-day operation around Hebron in the occupied West Bank, conducting searches, questioning suspects, and demolishing structures after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint. (AFP via Daily Tribune)
      • The Israeli government orders the military to prepare for a complete lockdown of the West Bank. (Al Jazeera)
  • 2026 Trappes and La Verrière shootings
    • A person is killed and five other people are injured in a drive-by shooting spree at three separate locations in Trappes and La Verrière, France. A suspect is arrested. The suspected motives behind the shootings are racism and Islamophobia. (BBC News)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Pacific typhoon season
    • Typhoon Champi kills a person and injures 163 others in Taiwan as the government evacuates 2,639 people from mountainous areas. (AFP via France 24) (Reuters)
  • Two Philippine Air Force (PAF) SF-260 aircraft collide during a low-altitude training flight and crash at Basilio Fernando Air Base in Lipa, Batangas, killing all four pilots aboard. The PAF grounds its remaining SF-260 fleet pending investigation. (AP)
  • An 18-storey building under construction collapses in Eastleigh, Nairobi, Kenya, leaving seven people missing and at least one injured. Rescue teams establish contact with some people trapped beneath the rubble. (AFP via The Australian)

International relations

  • Australia–North Korea relations, North Korean remote worker scheme
    • The Australian Government imposes financial sanctions and travel bans on two North Koreans and sanctions two companies accused of supporting fraudulent overseas information technology work that funds North Korea's weapons programs. (AFP via RFI)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Karak church shooting
    • Seven people are killed and 34 others are wounded in a mass shooting during a funeral procession at a Greek Orthodox Church in Hamoud, Karak Governorate, Jordan. All of the gunmen escape from the scene. (Al Jazeera) (AP)
  • The Eagle's Nest in Germany is destroyed in a fire. A suspect is arrested. (AP) (DW)

Politics and elections

  • Online age verification laws by country
    • The Greek parliament approves a law banning children and teenagers under 15 from using social media from January 1, 2027, requiring age verification and penalties for platforms that fail to comply. (Al Jazeera)

Sports

  • Argentine football player Lionel Messi is awarded the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports for his career at FC Barcelona in Catalonia, Spain. (OneFootball)

item.title: Current Events - October 16, 2026
item.description:
October 16, 2026 (2026-10-16) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Sudanese civil war
    • Thirty people are killed and 47 people are injured in a drone strike on a cattle market in Nyala, South Darfur, Sudan. (AFP via Dawn)
  • Israeli settler violence
    • Israeli settlers attack and beat a group of Palestinians and an American journalist from The Washington Post. (The Times of Israel)

Health and environment

  • Deforestation of the Amazon rainforest
    • Brazilian environment minister João Paulo Capobianco [pt] reports that deforestation in Brazil's Amazon rainforest fell to 5,796 km2 (2,238 sq mi) in the year through July 2026, the lowest level since 1988 except for 2012. (AFP via France 24)

International relations

  • Australia–Fiji relations
    • Australia agrees to provide Fiji with solar-, wind-, and wave-powered Bluebottle maritime drones and training for surveillance and efforts against drug trafficking and other transnational crime, with deployment expected in 2027. (AFP via RFI)
  • Hungary–Ukraine relations, Accession of Ukraine to the European Union
    • Hungarian prime minister Péter Magyar and Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy agree to improve bilateral relations during a meeting in Brussels, Belgium, with Hungary lifting objections to further European Union accession talks for Ukraine following progress on ethnic Hungarian minority rights in Ukraine. (Reuters)

Law and crimes

  • 2026 anti-CEC protests
    • Cockroach Janta Party leader Abhijeet Dipke is detained in Delhi, India, ahead of the party's planned march. (BBC News)
  • South African police rescue about 200 people from an unregistered rehabilitation centre in Mpumalanga and arrest two people while investigating alleged kidnapping and health and safety violations. Fourteen people receive medical treatment following the rescue. (Reuters)
  • A judge in Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico, sentences three Mexican men to over 158 years in prison each for the murder of two Australians and an American in 2024. (AP)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Moroccan general election
    • Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, who was named Prime Minister by King Mohammed VI on 29 September, takes office as her four-party coalition Government is formally appointed. (Morocco World News)
  • 2026 Czech Senate election
    • Czechs begin voting in the second round to elect 22 senators who were not elected in the first round. (Romea)

Sports

  • 2026 WXV Global Series
    • In women's rugby union, Canada defeats England 24–21 in a WXV Global Series match in Toronto, ending the Red Roses' four-year unbeaten run at 41 matches (the longest in rugby union history) after Shoshanah Seumanutafa scores a late try. (Stuff)
